signals.title: Nigeria : les familles des orpailleurs morts en détentions réclament justice
signals.summary: A Minna, dans le centre du Nigeria, les familles réclament des explications après la mort de 37 orpailleurs présumés alors qu'ils étaient détenus par le corps de la défense civile du pays. Le gouvernement a nommé une commission indépendante composée de dix membres pour mener l'enquête.

signals.title: Flood - Nema Urges Benue to Strengthen Preparedness
signals.summary: [Premium Times] NEMA has urged Benue to sustain flood preparedness and coordinate early warning, evacuation and emergency response as heavy rainfall continues.

signals.title: Angolan President Arrives in New York for UN General Assembly
signals.summary: [ANGOP] New York -- Angolan President João Lourenço arrived in New York, United States, on Sunday to participate in the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, where he is scheduled to address delegates on Tuesday, the opening day of the general debate.

signals.title: Malawi: Mozambican, Malawian named as suspected kidnappers shot dead in British national’s rescue
signals.summary:
Malawi Police have named the two suspected kidnappers who were shot dead during the dramatic operation that saw British national Nusrat Osman rescued from her captors in Blantyre. signals.title: Bandits Gun Down Mentally Ill Man, Abduct 28 in Sokoto Community
signals.summary: [Daily Trust] Sokoto -- Bandits killed three people and abducted 28 others during an attack on Kagara community in Goronyo Local Government Area of Sokoto State on Saturday night.

signals.title: Miners' Deaths - NSCDC Suspends More Personnel, Orders 3-Day Half-Mast
signals.summary: [Vanguard] The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) has suspended three more personnel and ordered three days of half-mast to mourn alleged illegal miners who died in its Niger State custody.

signals.title: Nigeria : des rescapés témoignent après la mort de 37 codétenus à Minna
signals.summary: Au Nigeria, des survivants de la détention de mineurs présumés impliqués dans l’exploitation illégale témoignent de conditions carcérales qu’ils décrivent comme insoutenables. Plus de 37 suspects sont morts, tandis que les autorités ont ouvert plusieurs enquêtes.

signals.title: Nigeria : Une commission d'enquête après la mort de 37 orpailleurs présumés en détention
signals.summary: Le gouvernement nigérian a créé une commission indépendante chargée d'enquêter sur la mort en détention de 37 orpailleurs clandestins présumés. Trente-sept jeunes hommes ont été retrouvés morts jeudi 17 septembre à Minna, dans le centre du pays, alors qu'ils étaient détenus par le Corps de sécurité et de défense civile du Nigeria. Les familles réclament des explications et que justice soit faite.

signals.title: Nine Killed in Plateau Communities, Troops Arrest 11 Suspects
signals.summary: [Premium Times] The fresh killings occurred between Saturday night and Sunday morning in communities in Barkin Ladi, Riyom and surrounding areas, according to community sources.

signals.title: Surviving Nigerian miners recount ordeal in detention after 37 deaths
signals.summary: 37 individuals, suspected of working as illegal miners, died in custody in Nigeria in recent days, prompting the government to name a committee to investigate the situation. The survivors recount their harrowing ordeal in detention.

signals.title: My Wife Miraculously Woke Up After Six Months in Coma - Akpabio
signals.summary: [Premium Times] The Senate president said his wife underwent a failed surgery and was declared 98 per cent dead while in a coma.

signals.title: Arrêt sur images du 18 septembre 2026 : au Nigeria, la détresse des proches de mineurs
signals.summary: Vendredi, dans le centre du Nigeria, la police a tiré des gaz lacrymogènes sur des manifestants qui s'étaient rassemblés pour dénoncer la mort de 37 mineurs alors qu'ils étaient en garde à vue pour exploitation minière illégale.

signals.title: Cameroun: les structures sanitaires sous pression avec des patients fuyant l’insécurité autour de Mora
signals.summary: Au Cameroun, après l'attaque jihadiste dans la nuit de mercredi à jeudi 17 septembre, qui a fait quinze morts à Makary dans la région de l'extrême-nord, plusieurs centaines de personnes ont quitté l'endroit pour se diriger vers Kousseri. Plus loin, à 174 km, dans la localité de Mora, proche de la frontière nigériane, des mouvements similaires de populations ont souvent été enregistrés après les attaques de Boko Haram dans les villages environnants. Avec comme conséquence,…

signals.title: Rescue Efforts Underway After Building Collapse in Maomboleo, Kisumu
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Kisumu -- Rescue efforts are underway after a building collapsed in Maomboleo, Kisumu, with emergency response teams heading to the scene.

signals.title: Miners' Deaths - NSCDC Parades Suspended Commandant, Nabs More Personnel
signals.summary: [Daily Trust] The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) has paraded Commandant Suberu Aniviye, who was earlier suspended over the deaths of suspected illegal miners in the Corps' custody in Niger State.

signals.title: Miners' Deaths - Shehu Sani Narrates 'Hell On Earth' Experience in Congested Cell
signals.summary: [Daily Trust] Former Kaduna Central Senator, Shehu Sani, has expressed sympathy over the recent deaths of 37 artisanal miners in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Minna, Niger State.

signals.title: President Extends Madlanga Commission's Final Report Deadline
signals.summary: [SAnews.gov.za] President Cyril Ramaphosa has granted the Madlanga Commission a final extension to submit its final report.

signals.title: Govt Probes Deaths of 37 Suspected Illegal Miners in Minna, Names 20 Suspended NSCDC Officers
signals.summary: [This Day] The federal government has constituted a 10-member independent committee to investigate the deaths of the 37 suspected illegal miners detained last Thursday by the Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Minna, the Niger State capital.

signals.title: 37 Miners' Deaths - Survivors' Account of Sprayed Substance Cannot Be Ruled Out - Niger Governor
signals.summary: [Leadership] Niger State governor, Mohammed Umaru Bago, said the account of survivors alleging that a substance was sprayed inside the detention facility where suspected illegal miners were held cannot be ruled out pending the outcome of investigations.

signals.title: Nigeria: Families demand justice for 37 men who died in custody
signals.summary: Families of some of the people who died in a Nigerian paramilitary civil defence force holding cell, on Saturday demanded justice as government appointed an independent panel to probe the deaths.

signals.title: RDC: après la mort de Miguel Masaisai, des dizaines de cyclistes lui rendent hommage à Goma et à Kinshasa
signals.summary: Pour honorer la mémoire du jeune sportif dont le projet « Pédaler pour la paix » était très suivi sur les réseaux sociaux, des dizaines de cyclistes se sont notamment rassemblés sur l'esplanade du Palais du peuple, dans la capitale congolaise, dimanche 20 septembre. Miguel Masaisai est décédé vendredi dans un accident de la route à Ouésso, dans le nord de la République du Congo.

signals.title: RDC : à Goma, le deuil après le décès du cycliste Miguel Masaïsaï
signals.summary: Miguel Masaïsaï est mort dans un accident de la circulation au Congo-Brazzaville alors qu’il traversait l’Afrique à vélo pour promouvoir la paix. À Goma, sa ville natale, famille, amis et compagnons de route rendent hommage à un jeune sportif engagé dont le périple devait s’achever au Maroc.

signals.title: Angola reactiva Plano de Contigência face à nova vaga de Mpox
signals.summary: A nova vaga de Mpox leva Angola a reactivar o Plano Nacional de Contingência. O país já contabiliza 593 casos confirmados e dois mortos, com Cabinda e Moxico Leste entre as províncias mais afectadas. Para reforçar a resposta ao surto, foram mobilizadas 50 mil doses de vacina, destinadas aos contactos dos casos confirmados e aos profissionais de saúde.

signals.title: Nigeria appoints panel to probe deaths of 37 miners in holding cell
signals.summary: Nigeria's government has appointed a 10-member independent panel to investigate the deaths of 37 people in a paramilitary civil defence force holding cell, the interior minister said Saturday.

signals.title: Mali : le bilan de l’attaque des jihadistes à Dioura s’alourdit à une centaine de militaires tués
signals.summary: Au Mali, le bilan de l’attaque menée le 10 septembre 2026 par les jihadistes du Jnim, liés à al-Qaïda, contre le camp de l’armée à Dioura, dans la région de Mopti, s’alourdit. Selon plusieurs sources, au moins 100 militaires maliens ont été tués, soit deux fois plus que les premières estimations recueillies sur le terrain. Plusieurs dizaines d’autres soldats ont été faits prisonniers par les jihadistes.

signals.title: Nigeria : après la mort de 37 mineurs, leurs proches réclament des réponses
signals.summary: La mort de 37 hommes détenus après une opération contre l’exploitation minière clandestine a déclenché de violentes manifestations à Minna, dans l’État du Niger. Des survivants affirment avoir été entassés dans des cellules sans ventilation, où plusieurs détenus se seraient effondrés.

signals.title: Nigeria gold miner deaths spark protests in Niger state
signals.summary: Survivors of a Nigerian disaster that saw 37 suspected illegal gold miners die while in the custody of a paramilitary civil defence group recounted their panic on Friday as they struggled to breathe inside the cell.

signals.title: South Africa: Olifantsfontein residents hold vigil for woman found dead
signals.summary: Residents of Olifantsfontein gathered to remember a woman whose body was found floating in a river in Clayville, east of Johannesburg, as communities across the area demand action over a series of killings of women.

signals.title: Guerre des drones au Mali, interview exclusive de Fouzi Lekjaâ, les secrets du renseignement camerounais… Les 5 infos qu’il ne fallait pas manquer
signals.summary: Cette semaine, le Brief de Jeune Afrique enquête sur les victimes civiles des frappes de drones au Mali, revient sur les ambitions politiques de Fouzi Lekjaâ au Maroc, dévoile les dessous de la guerre des clans qui fragilise les services de renseignements camerounais, décrypte les affrontements entre opposition et partisans du pouvoir en RDC et analyse les conséquences de la faillite de la Samir sur la politique énergétique marocaine.

signals.title: Kenya : deux morts après le crash d’un avion lors d’un vol d’entraînement
signals.summary: Un élève pilote et son instructeur ont péri vendredi dans le crash de leur petit avion lors d’un vol d’entraînement, dans le comté de Kajiado, au sud du Kenya. L’appareil s’est écrasé à proximité d’éoliennes et d’un établissement scolaire, suscitant l’inquiétude des habitants.

signals.title: Student pilot and flight instructor killed in Kenya plane crash near wind turbines
signals.summary: The aircraft went down near wind turbines in Kipeto, a hilly area of Kajiado County southwest of Nairobi, according to Kajiado West police commander Maureen Kuto. Neither victim was immediately identified.

signals.title: La mort de 37 mineurs en détention provoque des émeutes à Minna
signals.summary: Un couvre-feu de 24 heures a été instauré à Minna, dans le centre du Nigeria, après des manifestations et des violences déclenchées par la mort de 37 mineurs d’or présumés clandestins alors qu’ils étaient détenus par les services de défense civile.

signals.title: Nigeria probes deaths of 37 suspected illegal miners in custody
signals.summary: Nigeria's government suspended a civil defence commander as President Bola Tinubu ordered a "thorough", "urgent and "full and transparent investigation" over Thursday's deaths.

signals.title: Grim discoveries of murdered women spark fear in South Africa
signals.summary: Dineo Motapane is one of nine recent victims whose deaths have left a nation traumatised over the level of violence against women.

signals.title: Nigeria : les forces de sécurité déployées à Minna après la mort de 37 mineurs
signals.summary: L’incident a provoqué des émeutes à Minna, capitale de l’État du Niger, où les décès sont survenus la veille. La police a ouvert le feu pour disperser la foule

signals.title: En RDC, l’ancien ministre Constant Mutamba poursuit sa dégringolade
signals.summary: Déjà condamné à trois ans de travaux forcés, en septembre 2025, l’ex-ministre de la Justice a été reconnu coupable de détournement de fonds destinés à l’indemnisation des victimes de la guerre de Kisangani. Il écope cette fois d’une peine de dix ans de prison et poursuit sa chute spectaculaire, un an après sa démission du gouvernement.

signals.title: Nigeria: Armed security deployed in Minna after deaths of miners
signals.summary: Armed security personnel have been deployed in the Nigerian city of Minna, where demonstrators have been taking to the streets, a day after dozens suspected illegal gold miners died while in custody.

signals.title: Dozens of suspected illegal miners die in Nigerian custody
signals.summary: Authorities linked the deaths to disease, but this has been disputed by intelligence reports and relatives of the accused.

signals.title: Kenya: Health workers increasingly concerned in wake of USAID cuts
signals.summary: In Kenya, the impact of USAID cuts is being increasingly felt. At least 24 deaths of HIV-positive sex workers in Kenya have been reported, who, like Beatrice, in good health until aid was slashed by the United States early last year, health workers say.

signals.title: Pressure Grows As Organisations Picket Outside Kempton Park Police Station
signals.summary: [Scrolla] A "Picket for Justice," backed by FEDUSA, Contralesa, SANCO and dozens of other organisations, is taking place at Kempton Park police station today from 8am.   The picket is part of a full day of action, including a march to Church Square and a meeting with runners at the Union Buildings, following at least nine women's deaths in Ekurhuleni since July.

signals.title: Afrique du Sud : neuf femmes ont été retrouvées mortes en deux mois
signals.summary: L’Afrique du Sud sous le choc d’un possible tueur en série.  En deux mois, neuf femmes ont été retrouvées mortes dans le même quartier, à l'est de Johannesburg.  Le président Cyril Ramaphosa a ordonné que l’enquête sur ces meurtres devienne une priorité nationale pour les forces de l’ordre. Les explications de Caroline Dumay, correspondante à France 24.

signals.title: At Least 17 Dead Following Road Accident in Zavala
signals.summary: [AIM] Maputo -- At least 17 people have lost their lives and two were injured following a road accident in Zavala district, southern Mozambican province of Inhambane.

signals.title: At least 37 illegal mining suspects found dead in Nigerian custody
signals.summary: At least 37 suspects arrested for alleged illegal mining were found dead in Nigerian security custody on Thursday, officials said, claiming a suspected disease outbreak was to blame.

signals.title: Afrique du Sud : 9 féminicides en 2 mois, la piste d'un tueur en série inquiète
signals.summary: Neuf femmes retrouvées mortes en deux mois, dans une même région d’Afrique du Sud. À l’est de Johannesburg, ces découvertes inquiètent les autorités et font craindre une possible série de meurtres.

signals.title: RDC : les équipes médicales face à une épidémie d’Ebola meurtrière
signals.summary: En République démocratique du Congo, les équipes médicales sont confrontées à des conditions éprouvantes alors que l’épidémie d’Ebola continue de faire des victimes.

signals.title: Fuel Tanker Explosion Kills Three, Injures 14 On Eldoret-Turbo Road
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- At least three people have been confirmed dead and 14 others injured after a petroleum tanker exploded along the Eldoret-Turbo road near Paul Boit Secondary School on Thursday night.

signals.title: Uganda Struggles to Save Newborns in Critical First 48 Hours
signals.summary: [Nile Post] Uganda is struggling to reduce newborn deaths, with health officials warning that babies with life-threatening complications are dying within hours of birth because some health facilities lack the equipment, specialised staff and neonatal units needed to save them.

signals.title: Two Terrorists Killed in Macomia
signals.summary: [AIM] Maputo -- The Mozambican Defiance and Security Forces (FDS), operating jointly with its friendly Rwandan military force, on Sunday killed at least two Islamist terrorists during clashes in Macomia district, Northern Province of Cabo Delgado.

signals.title: Au Nigeria, 37 mineurs en situation illégale retrouvés morts en détention
signals.summary: Le gouverneur de l'État du Niger, au Nigeria, a annoncé jeudi l'ouverture d'une enquête après la mort de 37 mineurs en situation illégale en détention. Les décès sont imputés à la surpopulation carcérale et à une ventilation insuffisante dans un centre de détention de la Défense civile. Le drame a déclenché des manifestations et le report du début de la campagne électorale.

signals.title: Greater Fluidity in Angola/China Parliamentary Relations Advocated
signals.summary: [ANGOP] Luanda -- The Speaker of the Angolan National Assembly (parliament), Adão de Almeida, projected on Tuesday (15) in Shanghai greater fluidity and regularity in parliamentary cooperation between Angola and the People's Republic of China, following the signing of the Memorandum of Understanding between the two legislative bodies.

signals.title: Secretary of State Highlights Banking Sector's Role in Financing Mining Industry
signals.summary: [ANGOP] Menongue -- Secretary of State for Mineral Resources Jânio Correia Vítor on Tuesday highlighted the importance of the participation of national and international commercial banks in the mining sector as a guarantee of the financial services required for its growth and strengthening.

signals.title: Public Works Minister Calls for Faster Rehabilitation of Cuito Cuanavale/Mavinga Road Section
signals.summary: [ANGOP] Cuito Cuanavale -- Minister of Public Works, Urban Planning and Housing Carlos dos Santos announced on Tuesday that additional equipment and human resources would be deployed in the coming days to speed up the rehabilitation of National Road 280, on the Cuito Cuanavale/Mavinga section.

signals.title: Angolan Secretary of State for Industry Visits Embrapa Units in Brasília
signals.summary: [ANGOP] Luanda -- Angolan Secretary of State for Industry Carlos Rodrigues visited units of the Brazilian Agricultural Research Corporation (Embrapa) in Brasília on Tuesday as part of a study mission carried out in partnership with the African Development Bank (AfDB).

signals.title: Afrique du Sud : une série de féminicides suscite l’émoi à Johannesburg
signals.summary: Neuf femmes ont été retrouvées mortes en deux mois dans la même zone de l’Est de Johannesburg. Les victimes étaient âgées de 20 à 30 ans. La police tente désormais de déterminer si ces meurtres sont liés.

signals.title: Medical teams in DRC face difficult conditions as the race to contain Ebola outbreak
signals.summary: Medical teams face brutal conditions as grave diggers work night and day to bury victims of the Ebola outbreak which continues to grip the Democratic Republic of Congo.

signals.title: Cica Calls for Dialogue Among Political Parties to Strengthen Peace
signals.summary: [ANGOP] Cazenga -- The Council of Christian Churches in Angola (CICA) on Tuesday in Luanda called on political parties to establish permanent mechanisms for dialogue and understanding across the country, with a view to the peaceful resolution of problems and the strengthening of peace.

signals.title: Morocco Beat Rwanda in Africa Youth Handball Championship
signals.summary: [New Times] Rwanda's U18 men's handball team opened their African Youth Nations Championship campaign with a 33-26 defeat to Morocco in Abidjan on Tuesday.

signals.title: Sernic Incinerates 1.3 Tonnes of Fentanyl
signals.summary: [AIM] Maputo -- Mozambique's National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) on Tuesday incinerated over 1.3 tonnes of fentanyl and an unspecified quantity of chemical precursors in Moamba landfill, in southern Maputo province.

signals.title: Mwanza Moves Before El Niño Rains Turn Roads, Bridges and Homes Into Disaster Zones
signals.summary: [Daily News] Mwanza -- WHEN heavy rains arrive, the difference between disruption and disaster is often determined long before the first drops fall. For Mwanza, where roads, bridges, drainage systems, businesses and farms can all face the consequences of intense rainfall, preparations for the anticipated El Niño conditions are already gathering momentum.

signals.title: 38 Dead Following 20 Road Accidents
signals.summary: [AIM] Maputo -- The Mozambican authorities have recorded 38 deaths as a result of 20 road accidents that occurred over the last eight months in the central province of Manica.

signals.title: Buchosa, Sengerema Activate Flood Response Plans
signals.summary: [Daily News] Mwanza -- BUCHOSA and Sengerema District councils have activated disaster preparedness plans following Tanzania Meteorological Authority (TMA) forecasts of heavy rains, with residents urged to take precautions against possible flooding and other weather-related hazards.

signals.title: One of Mondlane's Witnesses in Upcoming Trial Murdered in Morrumbene
signals.summary: [AIM] Maputo -- A member of the National Alliance for a Free and Autonomous Mozambique (Anamola), the political party led by former presidential candidate Venancio Mondlane, was found dead after being kidnapped by so far unknown individuals in Morrumbene district, southern province of Inhambane.

signals.title: 3 Years On, Morocco Earthquake Victims Still Wait for Help
signals.summary: [DW] Reconstruction has progressed in the three years since the 2023 Morocco earthquake, but some survivors are still living in tents. Locals are divided as to how successful it's been, and whether state aid is enough.

signals.title: Benin-Sapele-Effunrun Road - Quiet Engagement, Collective Action Delivering Results
signals.summary: [Vanguard] I joined representatives of the Delta State Government, Commissioner for Works (Rural Road), and Public Information, Mr Charles Aniagwu, the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC), led by the Chairman, Mr Chiedu Ebie, Esq., and the Managing Director/CEO, Chief Samuel Ogbuku, PhD, and other relevant stakeholders at Amukpe Roundabout, Sapele, for the flag-off of the emergency intervention and rehabilitation of failed sections of the Benin-Sapele-Effurun…

signals.title: Gas cylinder explosion sparks fire that destroys flat at Olympic Village in Maputo
signals.summary:
A gas cylinder explosion sparked a fire that destroyed a flat on the second floor of Block 17 at the Zimpeto Olympic Village in Maputo on Friday. According to Televisão Miramar, the incident occurred while the gas cylinder was being replaced. The domestic worker reportedly tried to alert her employer after hearing a strange noise…

signals.title: Protest As Hoodlums Break Into Female Hostel, Rape Student
signals.summary: [Daily Trust] Hundreds of students of the Taraba State College of Nursing Sciences, Jalingo, on Monday staged a peaceful protest following an overnight attack on one of the female hostels located outside the institution's premises.

signals.title: Police Cordons Off Kisumu Building Site After Eight Injured
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Kisumu -- Police have cordoned off a building construction site in Mamboleo, Kisumu, after eight people were injured when a six-storey building under construction tilted.

signals.title: Sénégal: les coupures de courant à répétition pèsent sur le quotidien des Dakarois
signals.summary: Depuis quelques semaines, Dakar vit au rythme de nombreuses coupures de courant, fait inhabituel dans la capitale sénégalaise. Si la banlieue était particulièrement touchée, les zones résidentielles ne sont pas épargnées et certains craignent que les délestages deviennent de plus en plus fréquents.

signals.title: Kisumu Building Collapse - Eight Injured, Two in Critical Condition
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Kisumu -- Eight people have been injured after a building collapsed in Maomboleo, Kisumu County, the Kenya Red Cross has said.

signals.title: Wetangula Urges Motorists to Exercise Caution After Maai Mahiu Crash Claims Four
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetangula has called for greater caution and discipline on Kenyan roads following the death of four traders from Chwele in a road accident at Maai Mahiu.

signals.title: CJID, NHRC Sign MOU to Strengthen Press Freedom and Journalist Safety
signals.summary: [CJID] The Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID) and the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) have signed a three-year Memorandum of Understanding to integrate verified data from CJID's Press Attack Tracker into the Commission's monthly human-rights dashboard.

signals.title: RDC: Amnesty International accuse l'AFC/M23 d'exactions contre des mineurs au Nord et au Sud-Kivu
signals.summary: Le groupe armé AFC/M23 se serait notamment rendu coupable d'exécutions sommaires, de torture, de travail forcé et de recrutement forcé dans des mines qu'il contrôle dans l'est de la RDC. Il se serait livré aussi à un trafic d'or et de coltan dont des sacs auraient été illégalement acheminés vers le Rwanda, dénonce l'ONG dans un rapport qui s'appuie sur de nombreux témoignages ainsi que sur l'analyse de photos et de vidéos.

signals.title: UN envoy visits displaced communities in eastern DR Congo
signals.summary: UN staffs traveled to Kimoka in North Kivu on Friday, in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, in an area controlled by M23 rebels, to assess the situation of returnees and their living conditions in conflict-affected areas, as the country also faces its worst Ebola outbreak.

signals.title: Le pic de l’épidémie d’Ebola en RD Congo n’est toujours pas confirmé selon Africa CDC
signals.summary: En République démocratique du Congo, le pic de l’épidémie d’Ebola n’est toujours pas confirmé, selon Africa CDC, l’agence sanitaire de l’Union africaine. Une position qui contraste avec celle des autorités congolaises, qui affirment depuis la semaine dernière que le pic a été atteint à la mi-août. Depuis son apparition en mai, cette épidémie est devenue la plus importante jamais enregistrée en RDC. Plus de 6 000 cas confirmés et plus de 3 000 décès ont été recensés.

signals.title: DRC: OCHA helps with response endeavours amid ebola outbreak
signals.summary: The Ebola outbreak continues to spread in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, where the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, OCHA, is helping response endeavours through rapid and flexible funding.

signals.title: After Niger’s coup attempt, Tiani is running out of people to trust
signals.summary: After the 29 August mutiny, the Niger junta leader appears more isolated than ever. He has grown deeply distrustful of his own army, placing his confidence in a handful of loyal officers and his Russian and Algerian allies.

signals.title: Kenya : les coupes dans l’aide américaine menacent la lutte contre le VIH
signals.summary: Sous une dalle de béton sans inscription, dans un cimetière de Nairobi, reposent les restes de Judy, une travailleuse du sexe kenyane séropositive, décédée quelques heures seulement avant de rencontrer l’AFP le mois dernier, une victime de plus des coupes dans l’aide américaine.

signals.title: Finale de la Coupe du monde 2030 : face aux ambitions du Maroc, l’Espagne menace
signals.summary: Depuis l’attribution du tournoi 2030 au trio Maroc-Portugal-Espagne, la question de savoir quel pays accueillera la finale oppose Madrid et Rabat. Une rivalité envenimée par la crise de Ceuta et la dégradation de leurs relations diplomatiques.

signals.title: Maroc - Israël : vers l’ouverture d’ambassades dans leurs pays respectifs
signals.summary: Un pas de plus vers la normalisation totale des relations entre Israël et le Maroc. L’Etat hébreu et le royaume chérifien ont annoncé l'ouverture de deux ambassades. Les deux pays avaient normalisé leurs relations diplomatiques en décembre 2020 dans le cadre des accords d'Abraham.

signals.title: Nigeria methanol poisoning outbreak kills at least 49
signals.summary: Residents have told the Associated Press that a locally made herbal alcoholic drink known as “Monkey Tail” is suspected of being linked to the outbreak. Authorities have not yet confirmed the drink as the source, and investigations are continuing.

signals.title: RDC : l'opposition dénonce la répression de ses manifestations
signals.summary: La police a tiré des gaz lacrymogènes et des coups de semonce et a arrêté des militants contre le changement de la Constitution mardi.

signals.title: Minister: Rwanda ‘not ready’ to extradite Burundian coup plot suspects
signals.summary: In 2015, Rwanda received Burundians fleeing after a failed coup against then president Pierre...

signals.title: GROUNDUP: This Eastern Cape town only gets water for an hour a day

signals.title: Government to Resettle Residents Around Dei Biopharma Plant
signals.summary: [Nile Post] The Minister of State for Investment and Privatisation, Aminah Mukalazi, on Friday, September 18, announced that the government would resettle families who own land and property around the Dei BioPharma Ltd medicines and vaccines campus in Matugga, Nansana Municipality, Wakiso District.

signals.title: Emirates signs MoU with Mozambique’s ANDITUR to support international tourism growth

France 24 a enquêté avec Forbidden Stories sur la situation de plusieurs migrantes africaines accueillies dans un centre de Yaoundé, après leur expulsion par l'administration Trump, en vertu d'un accord secret négocié entre les dirigeants des deux pays.

signals.title: How al-Amoudi broke Morocco’s only refinery

signals.title: Migrants expulsés vers l'Afrique: plongée dans la mécanique de l’administration Trump
signals.summary: Depuis le retour de Donald Trump, plus de 25 000 personnes ont été expulsées des États-Unis vers des pays tiers avec lesquels elles n’ont souvent aucun lien, parfois sur un autre continent que le leur. Parmi elles, des centaines ont été envoyées en Afrique. Au moins 12 pays africains accueillent aujourd’hui ces expulsés : des Vietnamiens en Eswatini, des Colombiens en RDC, des Guinéens au Ghana. Pendant six mois, RFI a enquêté, au sein d’un consortium de 24 médias…

signals.title: 202 Sudanese Refugees Return From Uganda On Voluntary Flights
signals.summary: [Dabanga] Khartoum / Kampala / Amsterdam -- A total of 202 Sudanese refugees have returned from Uganda to Sudan on two voluntary repatriation flights, arriving in Khartoum and Port Sudan. She and her husband are also named in a criminal complaint formally lodged with prosecutors alleging money laundering, tax evasion and other offences.

Premier arrêt, les impacts du conflit sur le tourisme. Guides touristiques, pisteurs, artisans, et les autorités sont unanimes : la guerre a ruiné le tourisme dans l’extrême nord du pays. À Maroua, les lieux touristiques, pics de montagnes, les lacs et les parcs ne sont plus autant visités.

Une visite durant laquelle Washington a pu manifester son intérêt pour la méga-infrastructure, qui sera à terme le plus grand aéroport d’Afrique. Faye, who became ECOWAS chairman in July, met Diop in Dakar on August 27 ahead of the former Senegalese defense minister taking office on September 1.

signals.title: Wafu B Women's Champions League Qualifiers - Edo Queens, Ampem Darkoa Seal Semi-Final Places
signals.summary: [CAF] Nigeria's Edo Queens and Ghana's Ampem Darkoa Ladies have secured their places in the semi-finals of the WAFU B Women's Champions League qualifiers after maintaining perfect records through their opening two matches in Ouagadougou.

signals.title: Malians Say Climate Change Is Making Life Worse, Call for Collective Action
signals.summary: [Afrobarometer] Majority support investment in infrastructure and renewable energy.

signals.title: Tuareg Rebels Release 22 Mali Soldiers - Sources
signals.summary: [Daily Trust] Tuareg separatist rebels on Sunday freed 22 Mali government troops, some held for more than three years, adding to a steady flow of releases in recent weeks, according to security and junta sources.

signals.title: Foreign Affairs Cautions Tijjaniya Pilgrims Against Road Travel to Senegal
signals.summary: [Ghanaian Times] The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has cautioned members of the Tijjaniya Muslim Movement of Ghana planning to travel by road to Senegal for pilgrimage to reconsider their plans, citing security concerns along some major routes leading to Dakar.

signals.title: Malian PM's Visit to Algeria Underlines Need for Mutual Security Goals
signals.summary: [RFI] The acting head of the Malian government, General Abdoulaye Maiga has begun a two-day visit to Algeria. It comes amid a thaw after months of tension. RFI spoke to Bakary Sambe, the Director of the Timbuktu Institute about the security situation and what the countries hope to gain from the meeting.

signals.title: Columnist, Activist Jailed for Seven Years After Three-Year Detention
signals.summary: [MFWA] After being in detention for more than three years, Columnist and radio host Mohamed Youssouf Bathily, popularly known as Ras Bath, and activist Rokia Doumbia, also known as Rose Vie Chère, have each been sentenced to ten years in prison, with three years suspended.

signals.title: Idi Amin's grandson fights at Commonwealth Games
signals.summary: The grandson of former Ugandan dictator Idi Amin has caused controversy at the Commonwealth Games after being disqualified for headbutting his opponent.

signals.title: What triggered the mass migrant crossings into Ceuta?
signals.summary: An estimated 60,000 migrants from Morocco have crossed into Ceuta, with dozens dying during the journey.
